methodology.token_conversion: 4 characters per token; JSON-heavy payloads rounded up ~15% for key/quote overhead.
methodology.output_sizing: Sized to typical draft length, not the API MAX_TOKENS ceiling.
methodology.prompt_caching: NOT modeled. Once on, expect 30-50% reduction on input portion of stable-context calls.
methodology.web_search_fees: Bundled into the Sonnet synthesis call. If the implementation uses Anthropic's web_search tool, add ~$0.05-0.10 per search.

products.name: Event Ops
products.cost_shape: Event Classifier is 87.3% of product spend. Input-heavy (full event snapshot, 264 events, 166 KB JSON sent to Sonnet each run).
risk_vectors: More events in the sheet (snapshot grows linearly)
Busier Gmail/Telegram (classifier fires more reliably)
Run frequency increase (2x = 2x cost)
Switching Gmail Reader from Haiku to Sonnet (4x that line)
scenario_d_levers: Snapshot narrowing: classifier input 45k -> ~10k tokens, per-call $0.165 -> $0.060
Deterministic prefilter on readers: cuts ~40% of low-signal calls
Prompt caching on stable classifier instructions: trims ~$0.50/mo

products.name: Venue
products.cost_shape: Prospect Finder is the unbounded line; everything else is event-count-bounded.
risk_vectors: Aggressive prospect research (3-5 Prospect Finder calls per event vs 1)
Multi-pass Sonnet matcher (one pass per shortlisted venue)
Confirmation Tracker upgraded to Sonnet (5x that line)
scenario_d_levers: Cache venue memory + voice rules in Drafter context (drop input ~50%)
Deterministic keyword classifier before Confirmation Tracker LLM
Cap Prospect Finder web bundle at 20k tokens

products.name: Newsletter
products.cost_shape: Revise + Generate = 86% of newsletter spend. All four LLM calls run Sonnet (Apps Script v11 hardcodes it). Output tokens are large (4k draft body).
risk_vectors: More revise rounds per issue (3 -> 6 doubles the Revise line)
Weekly cadence instead of biweekly (whole product 2x)
Longer issues (6k output instead of 4k)
scenario_d_levers: Switch Scrape Luma to deterministic HTML parse (drop entire $0.04 line)
Cache voice rules + Elements + past issues (Generate input 20k -> ~8k effective)
Add DRY_RUN flag to Apps Script for menu testing without billing

products.name: Speaker Prep
products.cost_shape: Bio Fetcher = 57% (web research synthesis). Panel Q runs per-event, not per-speaker. Deterministic skills are zero-cost on purpose.
risk_vectors: Multi-speaker events (5 speakers scales Bio/Detail/Brief linearly)
Regenerating panel questions 3x per event
Switching Detail Filler / Gap Detector to Sonnet
scenario_d_levers: Cache event brief + voice rules in Briefing Drafter (per call $0.033 -> $0.024)
Reuse Bio Fetcher output across Briefing + Panel Q (no second LLM pass)
Cap Bio Fetcher web bundle at 15k tokens (most bios don't need more)

products.name: Sponsors
products.cadence: 1 outreach push/month + daily Funding Watcher (30 runs/mo)
products.cost_shape: Prospector is 55% (web research). Funding Watcher is the only daily-cadence call site. Onepager output is large (4k tokens).
risk_vectors: Aggressive prospecting (30 candidates/push instead of 10): Prospector $1.05 -> $3.15
Onepager every candidate (10 instead of 3): $0.25 -> $0.84
Funding Watcher 4x daily instead of 1x: $0.30 -> $1.20
Funding Watcher escalated to Sonnet: $0.30 -> $1.80
scenario_d_levers: Two-stage Prospector (Haiku scan 50, Sonnet synthesize top 10): 5x funnel for similar dollars
Funding Watcher batched weekly with digest: $0.30 -> $0.07
Cache sponsor criteria + voice rules across Onepager + Outreach + Next Angle (-30% input)

products.name: Outreach
products.cost_shape: Cold Outreach Drafter = 39% (volume-driven). Warm Intro Finder = 31% (web research per call). Contact Ranker weekly so per-call expense bounded.
risk_vectors: Daily outreach pushes instead of weekly (whole product 7x: $1.54 -> ~$10.78)
20 cold drafts/week instead of 5: Cold Outreach $0.60 -> $2.40
Warm Intro Finder per contact instead of per shortlist: $0.47 -> $1.95
scenario_d_levers: Cache voice rules + outreach style + relationship-stage criteria (-30% input)
Move Stale Detector + Relationship Stager to deterministic SQL/sheet query (drop entire $0.09)
Batch Warm Intro Finder by contact cluster (3 contacts/search): $0.47 -> $0.18

caveats: Token counts are planning estimates; expect +/-20% variance vs measured cost-tracker output.
No prompt caching modeled. Once on, Scenario D drops to ~$4-5/month range.
Anthropic pricing checked 2026-05-22; refresh against model-cost-map.md if it changes.
Cadences assume 1 flagship event/month; flagship / Demo Day months can roughly 2x Venue+Speaker+Sponsors.
Newsletter cadence assumes biweekly; weekly cadence doubles that product to ~$2.20/mo.
Outreach cadence assumes weekly; daily would scale linearly to ~$6.50/mo at Scenario B volume.
Funding Watcher daily cadence is a design assumption, not a requirement. Weekly digest: $0.30 -> $0.07.
Web search calls billed per search if Anthropic's web_search tool is used (~$0.05-0.10/search).
Google API costs (Sheets, Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Drive, Slides) are $0 at VCW volume.
Apps Script execution time is unmetered (6-min quota is an engineering issue, not a cost issue).
Gmail Reader output is shared across products per model-cost-map.md control rule 1; cost attributed to Event Ops.
Approval gate, sheet writer, drift detector contribute $0 (deterministic Python).
Workspace Framework runtime is $0 (no paid model calls).
Sponsor Prospector and Outreach Warm Intro Finder are the two unbounded call sites; watch in cost tracker.
the operator's revise-loop habit is a real variable; 3 -> 6 revise rounds doubles the Newsletter product line.
One-time eval and backfill runs are separate; use Batch API for those (50% discount).
Output tokens are estimated against typical draft length, not API MAX_TOKENS cap.
JSON overhead is folded in at ~15% on top of the 4 chars/token base rate.
Char-to-token rate of 4:1 matches the audit; prose is closer to 3.5:1, JSON-heavy closer to 4.5:1.
These numbers do not include Workspace Admin's labor or Codex/Claude Code IDE seat costs.

02-quick-wins row 10 (input-hash cache) rises — Confirmation Tracker, Funding Watcher, reader reuse.

agents.name: gmail-reader
agents.purpose: Parse inbox threads and extract event-related signal as structured JSON.
agents.when_to_use: Start of event-ops pipeline, twice daily, to surface event signal from Gmail.
agents.not_for: Drafting or sending mail. Read-only inbox scan.

agents.name: telegram-reader
agents.purpose: Extract mentions, decisions, and event signal from the team Telegram channel.
agents.when_to_use: Run in parallel with gmail-reader at pipeline start.
agents.not_for: Sending Telegram messages. That is telegram-notifier.

agents.name: event-classifier
agents.purpose: Fuzzy-match inbox signal to existing Events Master Sheet rows. Proposes cell-level updates with confidence scores.
agents.when_to_use: Stage 3 of the pipeline. Reads both readers + the sheet snapshot.
agents.not_for: Writing to the sheet. Proposes only.

agents.name: sheet-writer
agents.purpose: Apply human-approved proposals to the Events Master Sheet with drift detection and audit logging.
agents.when_to_use: Only after approval-gate signs off. No LLM used.
agents.not_for: Making decisions. Pure execution from validated proposals.

agents.name: approval-gate
agents.purpose: Build approval digests and parse approve/reject replies from Telegram.
agents.when_to_use: Between event-classifier and sheet-writer. Every write goes through it.
agents.not_for: Auto-approving. Always waits on explicit human reply.

agents.name: drift-detector
agents.purpose: Block writes when live values changed since the dashboard last checked.
agents.when_to_use: Before every sheet-writer write. Protects manual edits.
agents.not_for: Resolving conflicts. Just logs and skips.

agents.name: confidence-scorer
agents.purpose: Standard confidence scoring and per-field floors. Triages the approval queue.
agents.when_to_use: After classifier proposes. Tags every write with a score.

agents.name: venue-matcher
agents.purpose: Rank venues against event needs (size, neighborhood, prior use, vibe). Returns top 3 with rationale.
agents.when_to_use: Given an event row needing a venue. Reads venue memory.

agents.name: venue-outreach-drafter
agents.purpose: Draft a booking inquiry email tailored to the venue. Gmail draft only.
agents.when_to_use: After venue-matcher returns top 3 and operator picks the target.
agents.not_for: Sending. Draft sits in Gmail waiting for human send.

agents.name: venue-confirmation-tracker
agents.purpose: Watch Gmail for venue replies. Classify confirmed, declined, asking, ghosted.
agents.when_to_use: After outreach is sent. Surfaces non-confirmed past 5 days.

agents.name: venue-prospect-finder
agents.purpose: Web research for new venue candidates by neighborhood and capacity.
agents.when_to_use: When venue memory has no good match for an event need.
agents.not_for: Replacing memory. Augments only when memory is thin.

agents.name: sponsor-prospector
agents.purpose: Find new sponsor candidates from web and CRM context.
agents.when_to_use: When the sponsor funnel is thin and the next event needs lift.

agents.name: sponsor-fit-scorer
agents.purpose: Rank sponsor prospects: industry fit, funding, audience overlap, community marketing intent.
agents.when_to_use: After sponsor-prospector returns candidates.

agents.name: sponsor-funding-watcher
agents.purpose: Daily scan of TechCrunch, Crunchbase, X for funding announcements that hint at sponsor warmth.
agents.when_to_use: Nightly. Flags warm trigger moments for the pod.

agents.name: sponsor-cold-outreach-drafter
agents.purpose: First-touch sponsor email with warm reference, subject variants.
agents.when_to_use: After fit scoring and approval to draft.
agents.not_for: Sending. Draft sits for human review.

agents.name: speaker-bio-fetcher
agents.purpose: Fetch speaker bio from approved sources (LinkedIn, company About, X profile). Structured bio with confidence.
agents.when_to_use: After speaker is confirmed and prep doc is copied.

agents.name: panel-question-generator
agents.purpose: Draft 5 to 8 panel questions tailored to topic, bio, audience.
agents.when_to_use: After bio is filled. Output goes into the prep doc.
agents.not_for: Final questions. Always reviewed by the moderator.

agents.name: briefing-email-drafter
agents.purpose: Draft the speaker briefing email: logistics, format, talking points, day-of contact.
agents.when_to_use: T-7 days from event. Tone-matched to the speaker.

agents.name: stale-relationship-detector
agents.purpose: Flag contacts past cadence threshold (founders 30d, investors 60d, casual 90d).
agents.when_to_use: Weekly. Drives the outreach digest.

agents.name: contact-ranker
agents.purpose: Rank contacts by goal fit, relationship strength, recency. Per-contact rationale.
agents.when_to_use: Given a goal: e.g. 'find 10 contacts who can intro me to crypto seed funds.'
agents.not_for: Cold outreach. Ranks warm and stale CRM only.

agents.name: reply-monitor
agents.purpose: Watch Gmail for replies, classify positive/negative/neutral/off-topic, propose CRM updates.
agents.when_to_use: Daily after outreach drafts get sent.
agents.not_for: Replying. Surfaces classification + CRM patch only.

agents.name: weekly-digest-builder
agents.purpose: Compose the Monday update across workstreams: event ops, venues, sponsors, speakers, outreach.
agents.when_to_use: Sunday night. Goes to Telegram + Gmail draft.

agents.name: skill-router
agents.purpose: Route unstructured operator requests to the right skill (event-ops vs venue vs sponsors etc).
agents.when_to_use: When a pod member fires a free-text request at the workspace.

agents.name: cost-tracker
agents.purpose: Track LLM spend per skill per month. Used for the pipeline KPI.
agents.when_to_use: Every pipeline run. Appends to a cost log.

agents.name: eval-runner
agents.purpose: Run sanitized fixtures and score outputs against golden answers.
agents.when_to_use: Before every skill version bump.

agents.name: secret-loader
agents.purpose: Read secrets from .env.local without ever logging values.
agents.when_to_use: Start of every script. Redaction-aware.

agents.name: voice-rules-loader
agents.purpose: Load community voice rules into every prompt that drafts copy.
agents.when_to_use: Start of every drafting skill.
agents.not_for: Generating copy. Just inserts the rules.

agents.name: entity-resolver
agents.purpose: Resolve people and companies across CRM, Gmail, Telegram. Dedupe with confidence.
agents.when_to_use: Anywhere a name needs to map back to a CRM contact.

agents.name: newsletter-status-reader
agents.purpose: Read-only adapter exposing newsletter v11 state (current issue, draft status, missing links, feedback).
agents.when_to_use: Read whenever you need to know if the newsletter is in flight.
agents.not_for: Rebuilding the newsletter. Wraps the existing Apps Script.

agents.name: promotion-hold-checker
agents.purpose: Pre-publish blocker for events missing venue, pricing, ticketing, partner approval, audience clarity.
agents.when_to_use: Before newsletter draft includes a featured event.

agents.name: Operator-vc-owner-evaluator
agents.purpose: Read the dashboard like a busy nontechnical VC founder. Return only what is confusing, risky to click, or missing a clear next action.
agents.when_to_use: Before demos or UI changes. Ask for a short list: unclear label, why it matters, and simpler wording or placement.
agents.not_for: Code, strategy, live approvals, or long rationale. Operator only points out confusion and cleanup.

retros.name: approval-gate-reliability
retros.goal: land Telegram approval gate that actually applies updates after operator reply
retros.outcome: digest 38 sent, operator replied 'approve 1 3 4', 3 approved + 1 rejected written to review handoff records; pipeline end-to-end validated.
worked: drain pending updates before digest send so fast replies are not eaten by the drain step
line-buffered stdout for live demo readability
redacted bot tokens in error logs
explicit 409 Conflict explanation when another getUpdates consumer is running
didnt: initial run lost the operator reply because drain step ran after digest sent
raw bot token leaked once into error log before redaction
retros.lesson: drain first, then send, then poll from the saved update id. Never log raw bot tokens.

retros.name: sheet-writer-row-placement
retros.goal: write new events after the last data row, not at the top
retros.outcome: fixed create_new behavior; new rows append after snapshot end instead of inserting against spacer column A.
worked: snapshot row tracking exposed the off-by-one against column A
drift detector caught the bad write in the dev sheet first
didnt: initial implementation appended against column A and ended up inserting at the top
retros.lesson: always compute new-row index from snapshot last row, never from first non-blank cell in column A.

retros.name: phase-3-pipeline-orchestrator
retros.goal: one-command orchestrator: pull, read, classify, approve, write, refresh
retros.outcome: run_pipeline.py runs the full flow; full test pulled 266 rows, found 0 new event signals, produced 0 proposals, wrote nothing, refreshed snapshot, exited cleanly.
worked: queue-file handoff makes each stage replayable
drift refresh after write catches manual edits
retros.lesson: design for the empty-signal case first; that is what the pipeline does 80% of the time.

retros.name: venue-workstream-fixtures
retros.goal: scaffold venue workstream with Luma-backed memory and configurable scoring
retros.outcome: venue-matcher returns 3 ranked venues for flagship dinner; outreach drafter produces Gmail draft payload; tracker exposes missing-feasibility fields.
worked: fixture-first approach kept the loop tight
scoring weights in JSON instead of hard-coded
didnt: second-rank venue (Venue Beta) needs manual contact lookup
no Gmail reply tracker live yet
retros.lesson: ship the matcher and the tracker together; matcher without tracker leaves the operator chasing replies in their head.

retros.name: sandbox-public-demo
retros.goal: build a real local sandbox so the framework can be shown without touching live systems
retros.outcome: operator-console, run-surfaces, workstream-products demos shipped with fake Gmail/Telegram/Relay/Luma/content-status/Events Sheet fixtures.
worked: fixtures match the real schema closely enough that the demo flows look real
VC demo script gives a click-through narrative
didnt: VC walkthrough is still a doc, not a wired button
retros.lesson: the only way to demo HITL ops to a non-operator is to make them click approve.

retros.name: newsletter-v11-rationalize
retros.goal: rationalize 19 versioned drafts into one canonical Apps Script
retros.outcome: named the canonical file public-newsletter-script.gs; documented drift between deployed sheet and code in bug-inventory.
worked: bug-inventory is the only diff doc anyone needs
cell-map shift to row 22 is now explicit
didnt: body of sop-current-state.md is still off-by-one for rows below 21
retros.lesson: version churn is fine, but the diff doc has to be the source of truth.

retros.name: luma-memory-quarterly
retros.goal: stand up Luma history as a memory primitive
retros.outcome: pull_luma_events.py + build_venue_memory.py + upload_venue_memory_sheet.py work end-to-end on real Luma data.
worked: one script per concern keeps each replayable
venue memory is read-once by the matcher
didnt: no schedule yet; runs are manual
retros.lesson: ship the script first, schedule second; never invert.

retros.name: atomic-skill-registry-spec
retros.goal: decompose every skill into atomic primitives
retros.outcome: spec doc only; deferred until 3 workstreams ship.
worked: forced clearer naming on framework primitives like approval-gate, drift-detector, queue-manager
didnt: scope crept; 97 atomic skills is too many to maintain right now
retros.lesson: defer atomic decomposition until the workstreams prove the surface area.

ops_entity.name: Workspace Ops Agent
ops_entity.role: Venture Community Workspace team ops agent. Runs the pipeline, surfaces approval digests, hands off to workstream skills, and never acts without explicit human approval.
capabilities: run the full event-ops pipeline end-to-end (pull, read, classify, approve, write, refresh)
trigger venue-workstream runs and surface drafts to Gmail
build approval digests in Telegram and parse replies
watch Gmail replies and propose status updates to the venue tracker
compose the weekly Monday digest across workstreams
report cost, drift incidents, queue depth on demand
what_it_does_NOT_do: send any email (Gmail drafts only, human sends)
write to the Events Master Sheet without explicit Telegram approval
update Relay CRM (read-only adapter, propose-only writes)
rebuild the newsletter (routes around v11 Apps Script)
make sponsor or speaker decisions for the pod
lessons_active: approval gate drains pending updates before sending digest (2026-04-29 fix)
sheet-writer writes new events after the last snapshot row, never against spacer column A
Telegram bot tokens are always redacted from request error logs
use Haiku for extraction and relay; Sonnet only for judgment; never default to Opus
ops_entity.to_chat: Start the local ops chat server with: python3 ./workspace-dashboard/scripts/ops-server.py
